title: edge-pdp-fallback-playbook
content:
Quick playbook: how the edge gateway should behave when policy decision points (PDPs) are unreachable or slow. This is intentionally rough - ops + platform planning doc to align on defaults.

Background:
- We have multiple enforcement loci: edge gateway, regional PDP, control-plane central PDP, and runtime hooks on inference nodes.
- Edge is the first choke point; cheap to scale, but limited attribute view. Need clear fallback semantics so customer traffic is not accidentally rejected for transient control-plane issues.

Goals for fallback behavior:
- Protect customer data and prevent high-risk actions even during PDP outages.
- Avoid global blast radius from conservative defaults that cause mass denying of traffic.
- Make behavior observable and reversible with simple controls.

Suggested default modes (ordered):
1) Normal: edge enforces RBAC allowlists locally; regional PDP consulted for ABAC when cache miss or when route configured for ABAC.
2) Degraded-soft: if regional PDP timeout or network error, edge falls back to cached RBAC + allow-with-constraints for ABAC routes: allow but tag request with degraded=true and route to safe-model variant or reduced QoS tier.
3) Degraded-strict: if control-plane signals sensitive override (eg. security hold) or cached policy says deny, enforce deny. This mode reserved for security-critical signals only.
4) Fail-closed: only for explicitly flagged routes (PII export, billing adjustments). By default we avoid fail-closed for common routes.

Operational mechanics:
- Timeouts: regional PDP sync timeout = 25ms, retry once, then escalate to degraded-soft. Edge should have circuit-breaker to stop calling PDP if error rate > 10% in last minute.
- Cache priming: on startup, edge agent must obtain and validate a signed policy snapshot before serving traffic. If priming fails, start in restricted mode (RBAC-only).
- Decision tagging: every response should include an X-Authz-Mode header (normal | degraded-soft | degraded-strict | fail-closed) for telemetry.
- Logging: log decision-id, policy-version, cache-hit boolean, PDP-latency-ms. Surface top N routes impacted in the console.

Policy scoping recommendations:
- Keep a small, performant RBAC allowlist for edge checks (roles -> route set). Keep JSON size < 128KB to avoid parsing impact.
- Extract ABAC predicates into concise attribute names and short TTLs. Example attributes: tenant_status, contract_level, model_safety_flag.

Audit and remediation:
- Decisions from edge and runtime must be emitted to central eventstore with policy-version; retain 90d for incidents.
- When degraded behavior is active > 5m for a route, auto-create an incident playbook run and notify on-call.

Developer ergonomics and testing:
- Create a lightweight local mock PDP binary for devs to run with edge gateway integration tests. Include toggles to simulate latency and errors.
- Add an integration test that replays policy delta streams and verifies cache priming and rollback.

Security constraints and exceptions:
- For high-risk customers, allow explicit per-tenant configuration: "always-fail-closed" lists or "route-to-audit-only" flags. These should be set via control-plane and require two-person approval.

Rollout plan (pilot):
- Week 0: implement X-Authz-Mode header and basic cache priming in staging.
- Week 1: enable degraded-soft for non-sensitive routes for 2 internal tenants. Monitor telemetry.
- Week 2: expand to 10 tenants and add incident automation.
- Week 3+: consider enabling for public routes with documented fallback behavior.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Product decision: default for degraded-soft is allow-with-constraints or deny? (ask product)
- How many routes are flagged "safety-critical" and require fail-closed? (data ask)
- Investigate using WASM sandbox for fast local attribute eval vs calling regional PDP. (owner: Omar)

References:
- PLAT-1427: attribute-change telemetry task
- infra/policy-signing-spec (WIP)
- slack:#plat-routing conversation from Jan 2025

Note: this doc intentionally focuses on operational defaults and safety posture. Detailed policy language and PDP internals belong in separate design docs.
